This file is a WORK ITEM for Wikidata P1814 (name in kana). It holds a Shinto shrine's Japanese label, its Wikidata item, the jawiki article URL, and the article's LEAD, plus an empty `<!-- ANSWER: -->` marker.

Your job: read the LEAD and write the shrine's reading in MODERN HIRAGANA into the ANSWER marker, in one of exactly three forms:
  `<!-- ANSWER: KANA: ひろしまごこくじんじゃ -->`  the reading, hiragana only
  `<!-- ANSWER: KATAKANA: ミシマノオオヤシロ -->`  the lead gives ONLY an ancient/katakana reading
  `<!-- ANSWER: NO_KANA: <reason> -->`            no reading for THIS shrine in the lead

The reading is normally the parenthetical right after the bolded name in the first sentence. Take the reading of the SHRINE NAME ITSELF — not a 通称 (common name), not a 旧称 (former name), not the reading of the town it stands in, and not a second shrine the lead happens to mention. Drop interpuncts and spaces. Do NOT romanize, do NOT translate, do NOT invent a reading the lead does not give — NO_KANA is the correct answer when it is absent.

Why KATAKANA is a separate answer and not just a reading: a katakana reading is the signature of an old import error that a separate cleanup is undoing, so it is recorded and deliberately NOT written to Wikidata. P1814 wants modern hiragana. A collector (collect_name_in_kana.py) rejects any answer that is not hiragana, so a katakana or romaji answer filed as KANA is simply thrown away — file it correctly instead.

SOME of these files are DISPUTED-READING items and say so in their own TASK block: they name two candidate readings, A derived from the shrine's English label and B taken from other shrines whose Japanese name is identical, and they exist precisely because those two disagree. On such a file the LEAD is the tiebreak and it OUTRANKS both candidates — if the lead gives a third reading, that is the answer. They also accept a fourth form, `<!-- ANSWER: GUESS: <hiragana> -->`, for when the lead states no reading but the other evidence picks a candidate. Do not choose the candidate that merely looks more regular: shrine names take irregular local readings, which is why the two sources disagree in the first place. The TASK block inside the file is authoritative wherever it differs from this instruction.

This file is a WORK ITEM giving a Shinto shrine or Japanese Buddhist temple its English Wikidata label - Stage 4 of docs/english_label_pipeline.md, the residual that the deterministic stages (kana romanization, identical-name reuse) could not name. The `<!-- KIND / JA / KANA -->` marker carries what is known; KANA is the authoritative reading when it is filled, and EMPTY when the reading is exactly what you have to establish.

Conventions, which are not negotiable - they must match the files this folds into:
  * shrine: `<Stem> Shrine` (Iino Shrine, Kushikino Shrine).
  * temple: `<Stem>-<suffix> Temple`, the suffix romanized from the KANA so the reading survives - the kanji alone does not determine it (誓願寺 せいがんじ -> `Seigan-ji Temple`; 清水寺 きよみずでら -> `Kiyomizu-dera Temple`). Accepted: -ji / -dera / -tera / -in / -an / -do / -bo.
  * MACRON-FREE Hepburn (`Kozen-ji`, not `Kōzen-ji`), no parenthetical disambiguator, no trailing period.

RESEARCH the reading (jawiki article, official site, Kokugakuin database). Japanese place and temple names have irregular readings, so do NOT romanize the kanji by guess. Fill the `<!-- ANSWER: -->` marker with exactly one of `LABEL: <the English label>` or `SKIP: <short reason>` - SKIP when the reading is genuinely unsourceable or the item is not a shrine or temple at all. Never invent a reading to avoid a SKIP.

Do NOT edit Wikidata yourself and do NOT edit any other file - collect_en_labels.py folds ANSWER into en_labels_sonnet.txt and the daily submitter drips it out. When ANSWER is filled you are done with this file.

This file is a WORK ITEM writing UNIQUE English descriptions for a group of same-labeled Wikidata shrines whose standardized descriptions would collide (label+description pairs must be unique on Wikidata). The `== Members ==` list carries each item's context (municipality, deities, existing descriptions). Write one short distinguishing English description per member into the `<!-- ANSWERS: -->` block after its QID, in the normal Wikidata register (no final period; capitalize only a proper noun, which for these means the leading 'Shinto' - measured 2026-08-05, the corpus is 11,487 'Shinto ...' to 1 'shinto ...'); leave a line empty if nothing distinguishing exists. Answers must differ from each other WITHIN the group. Do NOT edit Wikidata yourself - a collector turns answers into QuickStatements later.

Write one short distinguishing English description per member into the `<!-- ANSWERS: -->` block after its QID, in the normal Wikidata register (no final period; capitalize only a proper noun, which for these means the leading 'Shinto' - measured 2026-08-05, the corpus is 11,487 'Shinto ...' to 1 'shinto ...'); leave a line empty if nothing distinguishing exists. This file is a WORK ITEM for Wikidata P1814 (name in kana). It holds a Shinto shrine's Japanese label, its Wikidata item, the jawiki article URL, and the article's LEAD, plus an empty `<!-- ANSWER: -->` marker.

Your job: read the LEAD and write the shrine's reading in MODERN HIRAGANA into the ANSWER marker, in one of exactly three forms:
  `<!-- ANSWER: KANA: ひろしまごこくじんじゃ -->`  the reading, hiragana only
  `<!-- ANSWER: KATAKANA: ミシマノオオヤシロ -->`  the lead gives ONLY an ancient/katakana reading
  `<!-- ANSWER: NO_KANA: <reason> -->`            no reading for THIS shrine in the lead

The reading is normally the parenthetical right after the bolded name in the first sentence. Take the reading of the SHRINE NAME ITSELF — not a 通称 (common name), not a 旧称 (former name), not the reading of the town it stands in, and not a second shrine the lead happens to mention. Drop interpuncts and spaces. Do NOT romanize, do NOT translate, do NOT invent a reading the lead does not give — NO_KANA is the correct answer when it is absent.

Why KATAKANA is a separate answer and not just a reading: a katakana reading is the signature of an old import error that a separate cleanup is undoing, so it is recorded and deliberately NOT written to Wikidata. P1814 wants modern hiragana. A collector (collect_name_in_kana.py) rejects any answer that is not hiragana, so a katakana or romaji answer filed as KANA is simply thrown away — file it correctly instead.

SOME of these files are DISPUTED-READING items and say so in their own TASK block: they name two candidate readings, A derived from the shrine's English label and B taken from other shrines whose Japanese name is identical, and they exist precisely because those two disagree. On such a file the LEAD is the tiebreak and it OUTRANKS both candidates — if the lead gives a third reading, that is the answer. They also accept a fourth form, `<!-- ANSWER: GUESS: <hiragana> -->`, for when the lead states no reading but the other evidence picks a candidate. Do not choose the candidate that merely looks more regular: shrine names take irregular local readings, which is why the two sources disagree in the first place. The TASK block inside the file is authoritative wherever it differs from this instruction.

This file is a WORK ITEM giving a Shinto shrine or Japanese Buddhist temple its English Wikidata label - Stage 4 of docs/english_label_pipeline.md, the residual that the deterministic stages (kana romanization, identical-name reuse) could not name. The `<!-- KIND / JA / KANA -->` marker carries what is known; KANA is the authoritative reading when it is filled, and EMPTY when the reading is exactly what you have to establish.

Conventions, which are not negotiable - they must match the files this folds into:
  * shrine: `<Stem> Shrine` (Iino Shrine, Kushikino Shrine).

  * MACRON-FREE Hepburn (`Kozen-ji`, not `Kōzen-ji`), no parenthetical disambiguator, no trailing period.

RESEARCH the reading (jawiki article, official site, Kokugakuin database). Japanese place and temple names have irregular readings, so do NOT romanize the kanji by guess. Fill the `<!-- ANSWER: -->` marker with exactly one of `LABEL: <the English label>` or `SKIP: <short reason>` - SKIP when the reading is genuinely unsourceable or the item is not a shrine or temple at all. Never invent a reading to avoid a SKIP.

Do NOT edit Wikidata yourself and do NOT edit any other file - collect_en_labels.py folds ANSWER into en_labels_sonnet.txt and the daily submitter drips it out. When ANSWER is filled you are done with this file.

  * temple: `<Stem>-<suffix> Temple`, the suffix romanized from the KANA so the reading survives - the kanji alone does not determine it (誓願寺 せいがんじ -> `Seigan-ji Temple`; 清水寺 きよみずでら -> `Kiyomizu-dera Temple`). Accepted: -ji / -dera / -tera / -in / -an / -do / -bo.

Fill the `<!-- ANSWER: -->` marker with exactly one of `LABEL: <the English label>` or `SKIP: <short reason>` - SKIP when the reading is genuinely unsourceable or the item is not a shrine or temple at all. Never invent a reading to avoid a SKIP.

This file is a WORK ITEM for Wikidata P1814 (name in kana). It holds a Shinto shrine's Japanese label, its Wikidata item, the jawiki article URL, and the article's LEAD, plus an empty `<!-- ANSWER: -->` marker.

Your job: read the LEAD and write the shrine's reading in MODERN HIRAGANA into the ANSWER marker, in one of exactly three forms:
  `<!-- ANSWER: KANA: ひろしまごこくじんじゃ -->`  the reading, hiragana only
  `<!-- ANSWER: KATAKANA: ミシマノオオヤシロ -->`  the lead gives ONLY an ancient/katakana reading
  `<!-- ANSWER: NO_KANA: <reason> -->`            no reading for THIS shrine in the lead

The reading is normally the parenthetical right after the bolded name in the first sentence. Take the reading of the SHRINE NAME ITSELF — not a 通称 (common name), not a 旧称 (former name), not the reading of the town it stands in, and not a second shrine the lead happens to mention. Drop interpuncts and spaces. Do NOT romanize, do NOT translate, do NOT invent a reading the lead does not give — NO_KANA is the correct answer when it is absent.

Why KATAKANA is a separate answer and not just a reading: a katakana reading is the signature of an old import error that a separate cleanup is undoing, so it is recorded and deliberately NOT written to Wikidata. A collector (collect_name_in_kana.py) rejects any answer that is not hiragana, so a katakana or romaji answer filed as KANA is simply thrown away — file it correctly instead.

SOME of these files are DISPUTED-READING items and say so in their own TASK block: they name two candidate readings, A derived from the shrine's English label and B taken from other shrines whose Japanese name is identical, and they exist precisely because those two disagree. They also accept a fourth form, `<!-- ANSWER: GUESS: <hiragana> -->`, for when the lead states no reading but the other evidence picks a candidate. Do not choose the candidate that merely looks more regular: shrine names take irregular local readings, which is why the two sources disagree in the first place. The TASK block inside the file is authoritative wherever it differs from this instruction.

  `<!-- ANSWER: KANA: ひろしまごこくじんじゃ -->`  the reading, hiragana only
  `<!-- ANSWER: KATAKANA: ミシマノオオヤシロ -->`  the lead gives ONLY an ancient/katakana reading
  `<!-- ANSWER: NO_KANA: <reason> -->`            no reading for THIS shrine in the lead

The reading is normally the parenthetical right after the bolded name in the first sentence. Take the reading of the SHRINE NAME ITSELF — not a 通称 (common name), not a 旧称 (former name), not the reading of the town it stands in, and not a second shrine the lead happens to mention. Drop interpuncts and spaces. Do NOT romanize, do NOT translate, do NOT invent a reading the lead does not give — NO_KANA is the correct answer when it is absent.

Why KATAKANA is a separate answer and not just a reading: a katakana reading is the signature of an old import error that a separate cleanup is undoing, so it is recorded and deliberately NOT written to Wikidata. P1814 wants modern hiragana. A collector (collect_name_in_kana.py) rejects any answer that is not hiragana, so a katakana or romaji answer filed as KANA is simply thrown away — file it correctly instead.

SOME of these files are DISPUTED-READING items and say so in their own TASK block: they name two candidate readings, A derived from the shrine's English label and B taken from other shrines whose Japanese name is identical, and they exist precisely because those two disagree. On such a file the LEAD is the tiebreak and it OUTRANKS both candidates — if the lead gives a third reading, that is the answer. They also accept a fourth form, `<!-- ANSWER: GUESS: <hiragana> -->`, for when the lead states no reading but the other evidence picks a candidate. Do not choose the candidate that merely looks more regular: shrine names take irregular local readings, which is why the two sources disagree in the first place. The TASK block inside the file is authoritative wherever it differs from this instruction.

Fill the `<!-- ANSWER: -->` marker with exactly one of `LABEL: <the English label>` or `SKIP: <short reason>` - SKIP when the reading is genuinely unsourceable or the item is not a shrine or temple at all. Write one short distinguishing English description per member into the `<!-- ANSWERS: -->` block after its QID, in the normal Wikidata register (no final period; capitalize only a proper noun, which for these means the leading 'Shinto' - measured 2026-08-05, the corpus is 11,487 'Shinto ...' to 1 'shinto ...'); leave a line empty if nothing distinguishing exists. Answers must differ from each other WITHIN the group. Do NOT edit Wikidata yourself - a collector turns answers into QuickStatements later.

This file is a WORK ITEM for Wikidata P1814 (name in kana). It holds a Shinto shrine's Japanese label, its Wikidata item, the jawiki article URL, and the article's LEAD, plus an empty `<!-- ANSWER: -->` marker.

Your job: read the LEAD and write the shrine's reading in MODERN HIRAGANA into the ANSWER marker, in one of exactly three forms:
  `<!-- ANSWER: KANA: ひろしまごこくじんじゃ -->`  the reading, hiragana only
  `<!-- ANSWER: KATAKANA: ミシマノオオヤシロ -->`  the lead gives ONLY an ancient/katakana reading
  `<!-- ANSWER: NO_KANA: <reason> -->`            no reading for THIS shrine in the lead

The reading is normally the parenthetical right after the bolded name in the first sentence. Take the reading of the SHRINE NAME ITSELF — not a 通称 (common name), not a 旧称 (former name), not the reading of the town it stands in, and not a second shrine the lead happens to mention. Drop interpuncts and spaces. Do NOT romanize, do NOT translate, do NOT invent a reading the lead does not give — NO_KANA is the correct answer when it is absent.

Why KATAKANA is a separate answer and not just a reading: a katakana reading is the signature of an old import error that a separate cleanup is undoing, so it is recorded and deliberately NOT written to Wikidata. P1814 wants modern hiragana. A collector (collect_name_in_kana.py) rejects any answer that is not hiragana, so a katakana or romaji answer filed as KANA is simply thrown away — file it correctly instead.

SOME of these files are DISPUTED-READING items and say so in their own TASK block: they name two candidate readings, A derived from the shrine's English label and B taken from other shrines whose Japanese name is identical, and they exist precisely because those two disagree. On such a file the LEAD is the tiebreak and it OUTRANKS both candidates — if the lead gives a third reading, that is the answer. They also accept a fourth form, `<!-- ANSWER: GUESS: <hiragana> -->`, for when the lead states no reading but the other evidence picks a candidate. Do not choose the candidate that merely looks more regular: shrine names take irregular local readings, which is why the two sources disagree in the first place. The TASK block inside the file is authoritative wherever it differs from this instruction.

This file is a WORK ITEM giving a Shinto shrine or Japanese Buddhist temple its English Wikidata label - Stage 4 of docs/english_label_pipeline.md, the residual that the deterministic stages (kana romanization, identical-name reuse) could not name. The `<!-- KIND / JA / KANA -->` marker carries what is known; KANA is the authoritative reading when it is filled, and EMPTY when the reading is exactly what you have to establish.

Conventions, which are not negotiable - they must match the files this folds into:
  * shrine: `<Stem> Shrine` (Iino Shrine, Kushikino Shrine).
  * temple: `<Stem>-<suffix> Temple`, the suffix romanized from the KANA so the reading survives - the kanji alone does not determine it (誓願寺 せいがんじ -> `Seigan-ji Temple`; 清水寺 きよみずでら -> `Kiyomizu-dera Temple`). Accepted: -ji / -dera / -tera / -in / -an / -do / -bo.
  * MACRON-FREE Hepburn (`Kozen-ji`, not `Kōzen-ji`), no parenthetical disambiguator, no trailing period.

RESEARCH the reading (jawiki article, official site, Kokugakuin database). Japanese place and temple names have irregular readings, so do NOT romanize the kanji by guess. Fill the `<!-- ANSWER: -->` marker with exactly one of `LABEL: <the English label>` or `SKIP: <short reason>` - SKIP when the reading is genuinely unsourceable or the item is not a shrine or temple at all. Never invent a reading to avoid a SKIP.

  `<!-- ANSWER: KANA: ひろしまごこくじんじゃ -->`  the reading, hiragana only
  `<!-- ANSWER: KATAKANA: ミシマノオオヤシロ -->`  the lead gives ONLY an ancient/katakana reading
  `<!-- ANSWER: NO_KANA: <reason> -->`            no reading for THIS shrine in the lead

The reading is normally the parenthetical right after the bolded name in the first sentence. Take the reading of the SHRINE NAME ITSELF — not a 通称 (common name), not a 旧称 (former name), not the reading of the town it stands in, and not a second shrine the lead happens to mention. Drop interpuncts and spaces. Do NOT romanize, do NOT translate, do NOT invent a reading the lead does not give — NO_KANA is the correct answer when it is absent.

Why KATAKANA is a separate answer and not just a reading: a katakana reading is the signature of an old import error that a separate cleanup is undoing, so it is recorded and deliberately NOT written to Wikidata. P1814 wants modern hiragana. A collector (collect_name_in_kana.py) rejects any answer that is not hiragana, so a katakana or romaji answer filed as KANA is simply thrown away — file it correctly instead.

SOME of these files are DISPUTED-READING items and say so in their own TASK block: they name two candidate readings, A derived from the shrine's English label and B taken from other shrines whose Japanese name is identical, and they exist precisely because those two disagree. On such a file the LEAD is the tiebreak and it OUTRANKS both candidates — if the lead gives a third reading, that is the answer. They also accept a fourth form, `<!-- ANSWER: GUESS: <hiragana> -->`, for when the lead states no reading but the other evidence picks a candidate. Do not choose the candidate that merely looks more regular: shrine names take irregular local readings, which is why the two sources disagree in the first place. The TASK block inside the file is authoritative wherever it differs from this instruction.

This file is a WORK ITEM for Wikidata P1814 (name in kana). It holds a Shinto shrine's Japanese label, its Wikidata item, the jawiki article URL, and the article's LEAD, plus an empty `<!-- ANSWER: -->` marker.

Your job: read the LEAD and write the shrine's reading in MODERN HIRAGANA into the ANSWER marker, in one of exactly three forms:
  `<!-- ANSWER: KANA: ひろしまごこくじんじゃ -->`  the reading, hiragana only
  `<!-- ANSWER: KATAKANA: ミシマノオオヤシロ -->`  the lead gives ONLY an ancient/katakana reading
  `<!-- ANSWER: NO_KANA: <reason> -->`            no reading for THIS shrine in the lead

The reading is normally the parenthetical right after the bolded name in the first sentence. Take the reading of the SHRINE NAME ITSELF — not a 通称 (common name), not a 旧称 (former name), not the reading of the town it stands in, and not a second shrine the lead happens to mention. Drop interpuncts and spaces. Do NOT romanize, do NOT translate, do NOT invent a reading the lead does not give — NO_KANA is the correct answer when it is absent.

Why KATAKANA is a separate answer and not just a reading: a katakana reading is the signature of an old import error that a separate cleanup is undoing, so it is recorded and deliberately NOT written to Wikidata. A collector (collect_name_in_kana.py) rejects any answer that is not hiragana, so a katakana or romaji answer filed as KANA is simply thrown away — file it correctly instead.

SOME of these files are DISPUTED-READING items and say so in their own TASK block: they name two candidate readings, A derived from the shrine's English label and B taken from other shrines whose Japanese name is identical, and they exist precisely because those two disagree. Do not choose the candidate that merely looks more regular: shrine names take irregular local readings, which is why the two sources disagree in the first place. The TASK block inside the file is authoritative wherever it differs from this instruction.

Write one short distinguishing English description per member into the `<!-- ANSWERS: -->` block after its QID, in the normal Wikidata register (no final period; capitalize only a proper noun, which for these means the leading 'Shinto' - measured 2026-08-05, the corpus is 11,487 'Shinto ...' to 1 'shinto ...'); leave a line empty if nothing distinguishing exists. Answers must differ from each other WITHIN the group. Do NOT edit Wikidata yourself - a collector turns answers into QuickStatements later.

This file is a WORK ITEM for Wikidata P1814 (name in kana). It holds a Shinto shrine's Japanese label, its Wikidata item, the jawiki article URL, and the article's LEAD, plus an empty `<!-- ANSWER: -->` marker.

Your job: read the LEAD and write the shrine's reading in MODERN HIRAGANA into the ANSWER marker, in one of exactly three forms:
  `<!-- ANSWER: KANA: ひろしまごこくじんじゃ -->`  the reading, hiragana only
  `<!-- ANSWER: KATAKANA: ミシマノオオヤシロ -->`  the lead gives ONLY an ancient/katakana reading
  `<!-- ANSWER: NO_KANA: <reason> -->`            no reading for THIS shrine in the lead

The reading is normally the parenthetical right after the bolded name in the first sentence. Take the reading of the SHRINE NAME ITSELF — not a 通称 (common name), not a 旧称 (former name), not the reading of the town it stands in, and not a second shrine the lead happens to mention. Drop interpuncts and spaces. Do NOT romanize, do NOT translate, do NOT invent a reading the lead does not give — NO_KANA is the correct answer when it is absent.

Why KATAKANA is a separate answer and not just a reading: a katakana reading is the signature of an old import error that a separate cleanup is undoing, so it is recorded and deliberately NOT written to Wikidata. P1814 wants modern hiragana. A collector (collect_name_in_kana.py) rejects any answer that is not hiragana, so a katakana or romaji answer filed as KANA is simply thrown away — file it correctly instead.

SOME of these files are DISPUTED-READING items and say so in their own TASK block: they name two candidate readings, A derived from the shrine's English label and B taken from other shrines whose Japanese name is identical, and they exist precisely because those two disagree. On such a file the LEAD is the tiebreak and it OUTRANKS both candidates — if the lead gives a third reading, that is the answer. They also accept a fourth form, `<!-- ANSWER: GUESS: <hiragana> -->`, for when the lead states no reading but the other evidence picks a candidate. Do not choose the candidate that merely looks more regular: shrine names take irregular local readings, which is why the two sources disagree in the first place. The TASK block inside the file is authoritative wherever it differs from this instruction.

  `<!-- ANSWER: KATAKANA: ミシマノオオヤシロ -->`  the lead gives ONLY an ancient/katakana reading

The reading is normally the parenthetical right after the bolded name in the first sentence. This file is a WORK ITEM giving a Shinto shrine or Japanese Buddhist temple its English Wikidata label - Stage 4 of docs/english_label_pipeline.md, the residual that the deterministic stages (kana romanization, identical-name reuse) could not name. Conventions, which are not negotiable - they must match the files this folds into:
  * shrine: `<Stem> Shrine` (Iino Shrine, Kushikino Shrine).

RESEARCH the reading (jawiki article, official site, Kokugakuin database). Japanese place and temple names have irregular readings, so do NOT romanize the kanji by guess. Fill the `<!-- ANSWER: -->` marker with exactly one of `LABEL: <the English label>` or `SKIP: <short reason>` - SKIP when the reading is genuinely unsourceable or the item is not a shrine or temple at all. Never invent a reading to avoid a SKIP.

Do NOT edit Wikidata yourself and do NOT edit any other file - collect_en_labels.py folds ANSWER into en_labels_sonnet.txt and the daily submitter drips it out. When ANSWER is filled you are done with this file.

  `<!-- ANSWER: KANA: ひろしまごこくじんじゃ -->`  the reading, hiragana only
  `<!-- ANSWER: KATAKANA: ミシマノオオヤシロ -->`  the lead gives ONLY an ancient/katakana reading
  `<!-- ANSWER: NO_KANA: <reason> -->`            no reading for THIS shrine in the lead

The reading is normally the parenthetical right after the bolded name in the first sentence. Take the reading of the SHRINE NAME ITSELF — not a 通称 (common name), not a 旧称 (former name), not the reading of the town it stands in, and not a second shrine the lead happens to mention. Drop interpuncts and spaces. Do NOT romanize, do NOT translate, do NOT invent a reading the lead does not give — NO_KANA is the correct answer when it is absent.

Why KATAKANA is a separate answer and not just a reading: a katakana reading is the signature of an old import error that a separate cleanup is undoing, so it is recorded and deliberately NOT written to Wikidata. P1814 wants modern hiragana. A collector (collect_name_in_kana.py) rejects any answer that is not hiragana, so a katakana or romaji answer filed as KANA is simply thrown away — file it correctly instead.

SOME of these files are DISPUTED-READING items and say so in their own TASK block: they name two candidate readings, A derived from the shrine's English label and B taken from other shrines whose Japanese name is identical, and they exist precisely because those two disagree. On such a file the LEAD is the tiebreak and it OUTRANKS both candidates — if the lead gives a third reading, that is the answer. They also accept a fourth form, `<!-- ANSWER: GUESS: <hiragana> -->`, for when the lead states no reading but the other evidence picks a candidate. Do not choose the candidate that merely looks more regular: shrine names take irregular local readings, which is why the two sources disagree in the first place. The TASK block inside the file is authoritative wherever it differs from this instruction.

Fill the `<!-- ANSWER: -->` marker with exactly one of `LABEL: <the English label>` or `SKIP: <short reason>` - SKIP when the reading is genuinely unsourceable or the item is not a shrine or temple at all. Never invent a reading to avoid a SKIP.

Write one short distinguishing English description per member into the `<!-- ANSWERS: -->` block after its QID, in the normal Wikidata register (no final period; capitalize only a proper noun, which for these means the leading 'Shinto' - measured 2026-08-05, the corpus is 11,487 'Shinto ...' to 1 'shinto ...'); leave a line empty if nothing distinguishing exists. Answers must differ from each other WITHIN the group. Do NOT edit Wikidata yourself - a collector turns answers into QuickStatements later.

This file is a WORK ITEM for Wikidata P1814 (name in kana). It holds a Shinto shrine's Japanese label, its Wikidata item, the jawiki article URL, and the article's LEAD, plus an empty `<!-- ANSWER: -->` marker.

Your job: read the LEAD and write the shrine's reading in MODERN HIRAGANA into the ANSWER marker, in one of exactly three forms:
  `<!-- ANSWER: KANA: ひろしまごこくじんじゃ -->`  the reading, hiragana only
  `<!-- ANSWER: KATAKANA: ミシマノオオヤシロ -->`  the lead gives ONLY an ancient/katakana reading
  `<!-- ANSWER: NO_KANA: <reason> -->`            no reading for THIS shrine in the lead

The reading is normally the parenthetical right after the bolded name in the first sentence. Take the reading of the SHRINE NAME ITSELF — not a 通称 (common name), not a 旧称 (former name), not the reading of the town it stands in, and not a second shrine the lead happens to mention. Drop interpuncts and spaces. Do NOT romanize, do NOT translate, do NOT invent a reading the lead does not give — NO_KANA is the correct answer when it is absent.

Why KATAKANA is a separate answer and not just a reading: a katakana reading is the signature of an old import error that a separate cleanup is undoing, so it is recorded and deliberately NOT written to Wikidata. P1814 wants modern hiragana. A collector (collect_name_in_kana.py) rejects any answer that is not hiragana, so a katakana or romaji answer filed as KANA is simply thrown away — file it correctly instead.

SOME of these files are DISPUTED-READING items and say so in their own TASK block: they name two candidate readings, A derived from the shrine's English label and B taken from other shrines whose Japanese name is identical, and they exist precisely because those two disagree. On such a file the LEAD is the tiebreak and it OUTRANKS both candidates — if the lead gives a third reading, that is the answer. They also accept a fourth form, `<!-- ANSWER: GUESS: <hiragana> -->`, for when the lead states no reading but the other evidence picks a candidate. Do not choose the candidate that merely looks more regular: shrine names take irregular local readings, which is why the two sources disagree in the first place. The TASK block inside the file is authoritative wherever it differs from this instruction.

This file is a WORK ITEM giving a Shinto shrine or Japanese Buddhist temple its English Wikidata label - Stage 4 of docs/english_label_pipeline.md, the residual that the deterministic stages (kana romanization, identical-name reuse) could not name. The `<!-- KIND / JA / KANA -->` marker carries what is known; KANA is the authoritative reading when it is filled, and EMPTY when the reading is exactly what you have to establish.

Conventions, which are not negotiable - they must match the files this folds into:
  * shrine: `<Stem> Shrine` (Iino Shrine, Kushikino Shrine).
  * temple: `<Stem>-<suffix> Temple`, the suffix romanized from the KANA so the reading survives - the kanji alone does not determine it (誓願寺 せいがんじ -> `Seigan-ji Temple`; 清水寺 きよみずでら -> `Kiyomizu-dera Temple`). Accepted: -ji / -dera / -tera / -in / -an / -do / -bo.
  * MACRON-FREE Hepburn (`Kozen-ji`, not `Kōzen-ji`), no parenthetical disambiguator, no trailing period.

RESEARCH the reading (jawiki article, official site, Kokugakuin database). Japanese place and temple names have irregular readings, so do NOT romanize the kanji by guess. Fill the `<!-- ANSWER: -->` marker with exactly one of `LABEL: <the English label>` or `SKIP: <short reason>` - SKIP when the reading is genuinely unsourceable or the item is not a shrine or temple at all. Never invent a reading to avoid a SKIP.

This file is a WORK ITEM for Wikidata P1814 (name in kana). It holds a Shinto shrine's Japanese label, its Wikidata item, the jawiki article URL, and the article's LEAD, plus an empty `<!-- ANSWER: -->` marker.

Your job: read the LEAD and write the shrine's reading in MODERN HIRAGANA into the ANSWER marker, in one of exactly three forms:
  `<!-- ANSWER: KANA: ひろしまごこくじんじゃ -->`  the reading, hiragana only
  `<!-- ANSWER: KATAKANA: ミシマノオオヤシロ -->`  the lead gives ONLY an ancient/katakana reading
  `<!-- ANSWER: NO_KANA: <reason> -->`            no reading for THIS shrine in the lead

The reading is normally the parenthetical right after the bolded name in the first sentence. Take the reading of the SHRINE NAME ITSELF — not a 通称 (common name), not a 旧称 (former name), not the reading of the town it stands in, and not a second shrine the lead happens to mention. Drop interpuncts and spaces. Do NOT romanize, do NOT translate, do NOT invent a reading the lead does not give — NO_KANA is the correct answer when it is absent.

A collector (collect_name_in_kana.py) rejects any answer that is not hiragana, so a katakana or romaji answer filed as KANA is simply thrown away — file it correctly instead.

Write one short distinguishing English description per member into the `<!-- ANSWERS: -->` block after its QID, in the normal Wikidata register (no final period; capitalize only a proper noun, which for these means the leading 'Shinto' - measured 2026-08-05, the corpus is 11,487 'Shinto ...' to 1 'shinto ...'); leave a line empty if nothing distinguishing exists. Answers must differ from each other WITHIN the group. Do NOT edit Wikidata yourself - a collector turns answers into QuickStatements later.

This file is a WORK ITEM giving a Shinto shrine or Japanese Buddhist temple its English Wikidata label - Stage 4 of docs/english_label_pipeline.md, the residual that the deterministic stages (kana romanization, identical-name reuse) could not name. The `<!-- KIND / JA / KANA -->` marker carries what is known; KANA is the authoritative reading when it is filled, and EMPTY when the reading is exactly what you have to establish.

Conventions, which are not negotiable - they must match the files this folds into:
  * shrine: `<Stem> Shrine` (Iino Shrine, Kushikino Shrine).
  * temple: `<Stem>-<suffix> Temple`, the suffix romanized from the KANA so the reading survives - the kanji alone does not determine it (誓願寺 せいがんじ -> `Seigan-ji Temple`; 清水寺 きよみずでら -> `Kiyomizu-dera Temple`). Accepted: -ji / -dera / -tera / -in / -an / -do / -bo.
  * MACRON-FREE Hepburn (`Kozen-ji`, not `Kōzen-ji`), no parenthetical disambiguator, no trailing period.

RESEARCH the reading (jawiki article, official site, Kokugakuin database). Japanese place and temple names have irregular readings, so do NOT romanize the kanji by guess. Fill the `<!-- ANSWER: -->` marker with exactly one of `LABEL: <the English label>` or `SKIP: <short reason>` - SKIP when the reading is genuinely unsourceable or the item is not a shrine or temple at all. Never invent a reading to avoid a SKIP.

Do NOT edit Wikidata yourself and do NOT edit any other file - collect_en_labels.py folds ANSWER into en_labels_sonnet.txt and the daily submitter drips it out. When ANSWER is filled you are done with this file.

This file is a WORK ITEM for Wikidata P1814 (name in kana). It holds a Shinto shrine's Japanese label, its Wikidata item, the jawiki article URL, and the article's LEAD, plus an empty `<!-- ANSWER: -->` marker.

Your job: read the LEAD and write the shrine's reading in MODERN HIRAGANA into the ANSWER marker, in one of exactly three forms:
  `<!-- ANSWER: KANA: ひろしまごこくじんじゃ -->`  the reading, hiragana only
  `<!-- ANSWER: KATAKANA: ミシマノオオヤシロ -->`  the lead gives ONLY an ancient/katakana reading
  `<!-- ANSWER: NO_KANA: <reason> -->`            no reading for THIS shrine in the lead

The reading is normally the parenthetical right after the bolded name in the first sentence. Take the reading of the SHRINE NAME ITSELF — not a 通称 (common name), not a 旧称 (former name), not the reading of the town it stands in, and not a second shrine the lead happens to mention. Drop interpuncts and spaces. Do NOT romanize, do NOT translate, do NOT invent a reading the lead does not give — NO_KANA is the correct answer when it is absent.

Why KATAKANA is a separate answer and not just a reading: a katakana reading is the signature of an old import error that a separate cleanup is undoing, so it is recorded and deliberately NOT written to Wikidata. P1814 wants modern hiragana. A collector (collect_name_in_kana.py) rejects any answer that is not hiragana, so a katakana or romaji answer filed as KANA is simply thrown away — file it correctly instead.

SOME of these files are DISPUTED-READING items and say so in their own TASK block: they name two candidate readings, A derived from the shrine's English label and B taken from other shrines whose Japanese name is identical, and they exist precisely because those two disagree. On such a file the LEAD is the tiebreak and it OUTRANKS both candidates — if the lead gives a third reading, that is the answer. They also accept a fourth form, `<!-- ANSWER: GUESS: <hiragana> -->`, for when the lead states no reading but the other evidence picks a candidate. Do not choose the candidate that merely looks more regular: shrine names take irregular local readings, which is why the two sources disagree in the first place. The TASK block inside the file is authoritative wherever it differs from this instruction.

Conventions, which are not negotiable - they must match the files this folds into:
  * shrine: `<Stem> Shrine` (Iino Shrine, Kushikino Shrine).

RESEARCH the reading (jawiki article, official site, Kokugakuin database). Japanese place and temple names have irregular readings, so do NOT romanize the kanji by guess. Fill the `<!-- ANSWER: -->` marker with exactly one of `LABEL: <the English label>` or `SKIP: <short reason>` - SKIP when the reading is genuinely unsourceable or the item is not a shrine or temple at all.   `<!-- ANSWER: KANA: ひろしまごこくじんじゃ -->`  the reading, hiragana only
  `<!-- ANSWER: KATAKANA: ミシマノオオヤシロ -->`  the lead gives ONLY an ancient/katakana reading
  `<!-- ANSWER: NO_KANA: <reason> -->`            no reading for THIS shrine in the lead

The reading is normally the parenthetical right after the bolded name in the first sentence. Take the reading of the SHRINE NAME ITSELF — not a 通称 (common name), not a 旧称 (former name), not the reading of the town it stands in, and not a second shrine the lead happens to mention. Drop interpuncts and spaces. Do NOT romanize, do NOT translate, do NOT invent a reading the lead does not give — NO_KANA is the correct answer when it is absent.

Why KATAKANA is a separate answer and not just a reading: a katakana reading is the signature of an old import error that a separate cleanup is undoing, so it is recorded and deliberately NOT written to Wikidata. P1814 wants modern hiragana. A collector (collect_name_in_kana.py) rejects any answer that is not hiragana, so a katakana or romaji answer filed as KANA is simply thrown away — file it correctly instead.

SOME of these files are DISPUTED-READING items and say so in their own TASK block: they name two candidate readings, A derived from the shrine's English label and B taken from other shrines whose Japanese name is identical, and they exist precisely because those two disagree. On such a file the LEAD is the tiebreak and it OUTRANKS both candidates — if the lead gives a third reading, that is the answer. They also accept a fourth form, `<!-- ANSWER: GUESS: <hiragana> -->`, for when the lead states no reading but the other evidence picks a candidate. Do not choose the candidate that merely looks more regular: shrine names take irregular local readings, which is why the two sources disagree in the first place. The TASK block inside the file is authoritative wherever it differs from this instruction.

This file is a WORK ITEM giving a Shinto shrine or Japanese Buddhist temple its English Wikidata label - Stage 4 of docs/english_label_pipeline.md, the residual that the deterministic stages (kana romanization, identical-name reuse) could not name. The `<!-- KIND / JA / KANA -->` marker carries what is known; KANA is the authoritative reading when it is filled, and EMPTY when the reading is exactly what you have to establish.

Conventions, which are not negotiable - they must match the files this folds into:
  * shrine: `<Stem> Shrine` (Iino Shrine, Kushikino Shrine).
  * temple: `<Stem>-<suffix> Temple`, the suffix romanized from the KANA so the reading survives - the kanji alone does not determine it (誓願寺 せいがんじ -> `Seigan-ji Temple`; 清水寺 きよみずでら -> `Kiyomizu-dera Temple`). Accepted: -ji / -dera / -tera / -in / -an / -do / -bo.
  * MACRON-FREE Hepburn (`Kozen-ji`, not `Kōzen-ji`), no parenthetical disambiguator, no trailing period.

RESEARCH the reading (jawiki article, official site, Kokugakuin database). Japanese place and temple names have irregular readings, so do NOT romanize the kanji by guess. Fill the `<!-- ANSWER: -->` marker with exactly one of `LABEL: <the English label>` or `SKIP: <short reason>` - SKIP when the reading is genuinely unsourceable or the item is not a shrine or temple at all. Never invent a reading to avoid a SKIP.

Do NOT edit Wikidata yourself and do NOT edit any other file - collect_en_labels.py folds ANSWER into en_labels_sonnet.txt and the daily submitter drips it out. When ANSWER is filled you are done with this file.

  `<!-- ANSWER: KANA: ひろしまごこくじんじゃ -->`  the reading, hiragana only
  `<!-- ANSWER: KATAKANA: ミシマノオオヤシロ -->`  the lead gives ONLY an ancient/katakana reading
  `<!-- ANSWER: NO_KANA: <reason> -->`            no reading for THIS shrine in the lead

The reading is normally the parenthetical right after the bolded name in the first sentence. Take the reading of the SHRINE NAME ITSELF — not a 通称 (common name), not a 旧称 (former name), not the reading of the town it stands in, and not a second shrine the lead happens to mention. Drop interpuncts and spaces. Do NOT romanize, do NOT translate, do NOT invent a reading the lead does not give — NO_KANA is the correct answer when it is absent.

Why KATAKANA is a separate answer and not just a reading: a katakana reading is the signature of an old import error that a separate cleanup is undoing, so it is recorded and deliberately NOT written to Wikidata. P1814 wants modern hiragana. A collector (collect_name_in_kana.py) rejects any answer that is not hiragana, so a katakana or romaji answer filed as KANA is simply thrown away — file it correctly instead.

SOME of these files are DISPUTED-READING items and say so in their own TASK block: they name two candidate readings, A derived from the shrine's English label and B taken from other shrines whose Japanese name is identical, and they exist precisely because those two disagree. On such a file the LEAD is the tiebreak and it OUTRANKS both candidates — if the lead gives a third reading, that is the answer. They also accept a fourth form, `<!-- ANSWER: GUESS: <hiragana> -->`, for when the lead states no reading but the other evidence picks a candidate. Do not choose the candidate that merely looks more regular: shrine names take irregular local readings, which is why the two sources disagree in the first place. The TASK block inside the file is authoritative wherever it differs from this instruction.

This file is a WORK ITEM giving a Shinto shrine or Japanese Buddhist temple its English Wikidata label - Stage 4 of docs/english_label_pipeline.md, the residual that the deterministic stages (kana romanization, identical-name reuse) could not name. The `<!-- KIND / JA / KANA -->` marker carries what is known; KANA is the authoritative reading when it is filled, and EMPTY when the reading is exactly what you have to establish.

Conventions, which are not negotiable - they must match the files this folds into:
  * shrine: `<Stem> Shrine` (Iino Shrine, Kushikino Shrine).
  * temple: `<Stem>-<suffix> Temple`, the suffix romanized from the KANA so the reading survives - the kanji alone does not determine it (誓願寺 せいがんじ -> `Seigan-ji Temple`; 清水寺 きよみずでら -> `Kiyomizu-dera Temple`). Accepted: -ji / -dera / -tera / -in / -an / -do / -bo.
  * MACRON-FREE Hepburn (`Kozen-ji`, not `Kōzen-ji`), no parenthetical disambiguator, no trailing period.

RESEARCH the reading (jawiki article, official site, Kokugakuin database). Japanese place and temple names have irregular readings, so do NOT romanize the kanji by guess. Fill the `<!-- ANSWER: -->` marker with exactly one of `LABEL: <the English label>` or `SKIP: <short reason>` - SKIP when the reading is genuinely unsourceable or the item is not a shrine or temple at all. Never invent a reading to avoid a SKIP.

Your job: read the LEAD and write the shrine's reading in MODERN HIRAGANA into the ANSWER marker, in one of exactly three forms:
  `<!-- ANSWER: KANA: ひろしまごこくじんじゃ -->`  the reading, hiragana only
  `<!-- ANSWER: KATAKANA: ミシマノオオヤシロ -->`  the lead gives ONLY an ancient/katakana reading
  `<!-- ANSWER: NO_KANA: <reason> -->`            no reading for THIS shrine in the lead

The reading is normally the parenthetical right after the bolded name in the first sentence. Take the reading of the SHRINE NAME ITSELF — not a 通称 (common name), not a 旧称 (former name), not the reading of the town it stands in, and not a second shrine the lead happens to mention. Drop interpuncts and spaces. Do NOT romanize, do NOT translate, do NOT invent a reading the lead does not give — NO_KANA is the correct answer when it is absent.

Why KATAKANA is a separate answer and not just a reading: a katakana reading is the signature of an old import error that a separate cleanup is undoing, so it is recorded and deliberately NOT written to Wikidata. P1814 wants modern hiragana. A collector (collect_name_in_kana.py) rejects any answer that is not hiragana, so a katakana or romaji answer filed as KANA is simply thrown away — file it correctly instead.

SOME of these files are DISPUTED-READING items and say so in their own TASK block: they name two candidate readings, A derived from the shrine's English label and B taken from other shrines whose Japanese name is identical, and they exist precisely because those two disagree. On such a file the LEAD is the tiebreak and it OUTRANKS both candidates — if the lead gives a third reading, that is the answer. They also accept a fourth form, `<!-- ANSWER: GUESS: <hiragana> -->`, for when the lead states no reading but the other evidence picks a candidate. Do not choose the candidate that merely looks more regular: shrine names take irregular local readings, which is why the two sources disagree in the first place. The TASK block inside the file is authoritative wherever it differs from this instruction.

This file is a WORK ITEM giving a Shinto shrine or Japanese Buddhist temple its English Wikidata label - Stage 4 of docs/english_label_pipeline.md, the residual that the deterministic stages (kana romanization, identical-name reuse) could not name. The `<!-- KIND / JA / KANA -->` marker carries what is known; KANA is the authoritative reading when it is filled, and EMPTY when the reading is exactly what you have to establish.

Conventions, which are not negotiable - they must match the files this folds into:
  * shrine: `<Stem> Shrine` (Iino Shrine, Kushikino Shrine).
  * temple: `<Stem>-<suffix> Temple`, the suffix romanized from the KANA so the reading survives - the kanji alone does not determine it (誓願寺 せいがんじ -> `Seigan-ji Temple`; 清水寺 きよみずでら -> `Kiyomizu-dera Temple`). Accepted: -ji / -dera / -tera / -in / -an / -do / -bo.
  * MACRON-FREE Hepburn (`Kozen-ji`, not `Kōzen-ji`), no parenthetical disambiguator, no trailing period.

RESEARCH the reading (jawiki article, official site, Kokugakuin database). Japanese place and temple names have irregular readings, so do NOT romanize the kanji by guess. Fill the `<!-- ANSWER: -->` marker with exactly one of `LABEL: <the English label>` or `SKIP: <short reason>` - SKIP when the reading is genuinely unsourceable or the item is not a shrine or temple at all. Never invent a reading to avoid a SKIP.

This file is a WORK ITEM giving a Shinto shrine or Japanese Buddhist temple its English Wikidata label - Stage 4 of docs/english_label_pipeline.md, the residual that the deterministic stages (kana romanization, identical-name reuse) could not name. The `<!-- KIND / JA / KANA -->` marker carries what is known; KANA is the authoritative reading when it is filled, and EMPTY when the reading is exactly what you have to establish.

Conventions, which are not negotiable - they must match the files this folds into:
  * shrine: `<Stem> Shrine` (Iino Shrine, Kushikino Shrine).

Fill the `<!-- ANSWER: -->` marker with exactly one of `LABEL: <the English label>` or `SKIP: <short reason>` - SKIP when the reading is genuinely unsourceable or the item is not a shrine or temple at all. Never invent a reading to avoid a SKIP.

Your job: read the LEAD and write the shrine's reading in MODERN HIRAGANA into the ANSWER marker, in one of exactly three forms:
  `<!-- ANSWER: KANA: ひろしまごこくじんじゃ -->`  the reading, hiragana only
  `<!-- ANSWER: KATAKANA: ミシマノオオヤシロ -->`  the lead gives ONLY an ancient/katakana reading
  `<!-- ANSWER: NO_KANA: <reason> -->`            no reading for THIS shrine in the lead

The reading is normally the parenthetical right after the bolded name in the first sentence. Take the reading of the SHRINE NAME ITSELF — not a 通称 (common name), not a 旧称 (former name), not the reading of the town it stands in, and not a second shrine the lead happens to mention. Drop interpuncts and spaces. Do NOT romanize, do NOT translate, do NOT invent a reading the lead does not give — NO_KANA is the correct answer when it is absent.

Why KATAKANA is a separate answer and not just a reading: a katakana reading is the signature of an old import error that a separate cleanup is undoing, so it is recorded and deliberately NOT written to Wikidata. P1814 wants modern hiragana. A collector (collect_name_in_kana.py) rejects any answer that is not hiragana, so a katakana or romaji answer filed as KANA is simply thrown away — file it correctly instead.

SOME of these files are DISPUTED-READING items and say so in their own TASK block: they name two candidate readings, A derived from the shrine's English label and B taken from other shrines whose Japanese name is identical, and they exist precisely because those two disagree. On such a file the LEAD is the tiebreak and it OUTRANKS both candidates — if the lead gives a third reading, that is the answer. They also accept a fourth form, `<!-- ANSWER: GUESS: <hiragana> -->`, for when the lead states no reading but the other evidence picks a candidate. Do not choose the candidate that merely looks more regular: shrine names take irregular local readings, which is why the two sources disagree in the first place. The TASK block inside the file is authoritative wherever it differs from this instruction.

This file is a WORK ITEM giving a Shinto shrine or Japanese Buddhist temple its English Wikidata label - Stage 4 of docs/english_label_pipeline.md, the residual that the deterministic stages (kana romanization, identical-name reuse) could not name. Conventions, which are not negotiable - they must match the files this folds into:
  * shrine: `<Stem> Shrine` (Iino Shrine, Kushikino Shrine).
  * temple: `<Stem>-<suffix> Temple`, the suffix romanized from the KANA so the reading survives - the kanji alone does not determine it (誓願寺 せいがんじ -> `Seigan-ji Temple`; 清水寺 きよみずでら -> `Kiyomizu-dera Temple`). Accepted: -ji / -dera / -tera / -in / -an / -do / -bo.
  * MACRON-FREE Hepburn (`Kozen-ji`, not `Kōzen-ji`), no parenthetical disambiguator, no trailing period.

RESEARCH the reading (jawiki article, official site, Kokugakuin database). Japanese place and temple names have irregular readings, so do NOT romanize the kanji by guess. Fill the `<!-- ANSWER: -->` marker with exactly one of `LABEL: <the English label>` or `SKIP: <short reason>` - SKIP when the reading is genuinely unsourceable or the item is not a shrine or temple at all. Never invent a reading to avoid a SKIP.
